description: Unified document core (docx_engine) owns template tagging and filling; no generation logic in frontend.
Cross-run XML replacement: user-selected text spanning multiple runs tagged correctly.
Fill operation detects unclosed tags ({{) and returns structured error.
Template documents stored on filesystem; SQLite stores paths and metadata only.
Binary IPC replaces Base64 string bridging for large documents.
PDF export does not require LibreOffice; uses bundled/headless renderer.
Export formats: DOCX, PDF, HTML preview, .dfpkg bundle.
Template Creator: upload DOCX, define 5 field types, preview, save.
Template Filler: fill values, preview, export with inline validation.
Template versioning: draft/review/published/archived states and rollback.
RBAC roles: viewer, filler, creator, approver, admin.
Approval workflow: draft -> review -> published.
Immutable exportable audit log for all generation events.
Admin console for users, seats, licenses, audit logs, and reports.
Offline activation: Pro, Business, Enterprise signed offline files.
CLI, REST bridge, and webhooks for headless automation.
Strict CSP in Tauri; sanitized preview rendering.
DOCX validation, zip bomb limits, and path traversal guards.
Local DPAPI encryption at rest; zero-knowledge licensing.
Opt-in telemetry consent dialog; default deny.
SSO/SAML authentication and on-prem air-gapped builds.
Signed auto-update, staged rollout, and SBOM generation.
A Bundle is a reusable generation definition: identity, documents, canonical field schema, mappings, rules, output configuration, and a version history.
Published Bundle Versions are immutable; any change creates a new version and every generation references the exact version used.
Bundle import/export works via a portable .dfpkg package; no cloud is required.

Canonical field schema supports 13 types (text, multiline_text, number, currency, percentage, date, datetime, boolean, email, phone, url, select, multiselect) with attributes id, label, description, type, required, default, validation, group, options, format.
Field groups have shared vs document-specific scope; the UI presents them as separate sections.
An explicit deterministic mapping layer links every document placeholder to a canonical field.
A Matter is an instance of a Bundle Version; matter data is stored separately from the bundle definition.
One matter data source feeds many generated documents; no per-document re-entry.
Matter creation UX: select bundle, grouped form, validate, preview, generate.
Validation operates at three levels: field, matter, bundle.
A Generation Run records id, matter_id, bundle_id, bundle_version, timestamp, input snapshot, engine version, output files, warnings, errors, status.
Historical generated documents are never mutated; a change creates a new run.
Generation supports all or selected documents, deterministic output naming rules, and DOCX/PDF output.
Conditional documents are declared at bundle level with a generation preview explaining skipped documents.
Rule conditions use a safe deterministic expression system; no unrestricted scripting.
Bundle Health Check diagnostics identify the exact document and field.
Professional neutrality: no hard-coded legal or company-secretarial rules in the core domain model.
No frontend generation engine; the Rust docx_engine remains the single source of truth.
